szoveg_eredeti:
On 26 October 2026, the UNESCO Regional Office in Santiago signed a cooperation agreement with Efekta Education Group, a company belonging to the EF (Education First) group, which has joined the Observatory on Artificial Intelligence in Education for Latin America and the Caribbean as a new partner.

The signing took place in Santiago and was attended by Esther Kuisch Laroche, Director of the UNESCO Regional Office in Santiago, and an Efekta delegation led by its Global President, Peter Burman.

The agreement forms part of UNESCO’s efforts to promote the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education in ways that respond to the needs of education systems in the region, with particular attention to equity, inclusion and the strengthening of teachers’ capacities.

Launched in April 2026, the Observatory on Artificial Intelligence in Education for Latin America and the Caribbean is a regional platform coordinated by UNESCO Santiago that seeks to contribute to the responsible and equitable governance of artificial intelligence in education.

Its work is structured around three main areas: generating evidence to inform decision-making and education policies; developing the capacities of teachers and policy-makers; and promoting innovation and the exchange of knowledge and experiences among countries in the region.

Efekta’s participation expands the Observatory’s network of collaboration and opens up new opportunities to explore applications of artificial intelligence that can support teaching and learning processes.

Efekta Education Group develops AI-based educational technologies, including a digital tutor for students and support tools for teachers, primarily focused on English-language learning. Its platform has reached more than 24 million students in 179 countries.

This article is related to the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.
